channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Desaprovação do governo Lula chega a 63,5% no Paraná
item.description: A Paraná Pesquisas survey released on April 14, 2026, shows 63.5% of voters in Paraná disapprove of President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s government, with 32.8% approving and 3.7% undecided. Conducted from April 10–12 among 1,500 respondents across 56 municipalities, the poll has a 2.6 percentage point margin of error and 95% confidence level. The study was funded by the Liberal Party and registered with the TSE under BR-02080/2026.

item.title: O bengalão
item.description: STF ministers see themselves as pillars of democracy and view criticism of the Court as an attack on the regime, especially after the Bolsonaro government, which sought to weaken the Supreme Court to enable a coup. During that period, heterodox interpretations by the justices were incorporated into the legal system and accepted by society as necessary to neutralize the institutional threat.

item.title: Se eleições fossem hoje, Flávio venceria Lula no 1º turno no Paraná
item.description: A Paraná Pesquisas survey released on April 14, 2026, indicates that Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) would defeat Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) in the first round of the presidential election in Paraná, with 48.2% voting intention versus Lula’s 25.1%. In a hypothetical second-round scenario, Bolsonaro would lead 58.1% to Lula’s 29.8%. The poll, registered with the TSE under BR-02080/2026, surveyed 1,500 people from April 10–12, 2026, with a margin of error of ±2.6 percentage points and 95% confidence level, and was funded by the Liberal Party.

item.title: O estado onde Flávio Bolsonaro tem vantagem de quase 30 pontos sobre Lula
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro leads voting intentions in Paraná with 48.2% in the first round and 58.1% in the second round against Lula, who has 25.1% and 29.8%, respectively. The Paraná Pesquisas survey shows 63.5% of Paraná voters disapprove of Lula’s government, reinforcing Bolsonaro’s advantage. Sergio Moro also leads the state race in Paraná.

item.title: Datafolha: 75% afirmam que ministros do STF têm poder demais, e 71% veem Corte essencial para a democracia
item.description: A Datafolha survey shows 75% of Brazilians believe STF ministers have too much power, while 71% see the Court as essential for democracy. Distrust in the STF reached a record 43%, with the highest rejection among Bolsonaro voters (88%), though 64% of Lula voters also perceive excessive power. Despite criticism, a majority still acknowledges the Court’s institutional role in defending democracy.

item.title: Daniel Vilela lidera cenários para governador de Goiás, diz Gerp
item.description: Governor Daniel Vilela (MDB) leads all scenarios for re-election in Goiás according to a Gerp poll released on April 14, 2026, with 42% to 45% in the first round and up to 68% in second-round scenarios. The survey interviewed 1,206 voters between April 6 and 10, with a 2.88 percentage point margin of error and 95% confidence level. Vilela has low rejection (5%), while Adriana Accorsi (PT) and Marconi Perillo (PSDB) are the most rejected, at 39% and 31%.

item.title: Lula vai à Europa com comitiva de 14 ministros e 30 acordos em vista
item.description: President Lula travels to Europe with 14 ministers to secure over 30 agreements, mainly with Spain and Germany, aiming to strengthen the Mercosul-EU deal, promote democracy, and advance Brazil's reindustrialization agenda. The trip includes a bilateral summit in Barcelona, a Democracy Forum with leaders from 16 countries, and meetings with business leaders from key sectors.

item.title: Gracinha Caiado lidera disputa pelo Senado em Goiás, diz pesquisa
item.description: Gracinha Caiado (União Brasil) leads the Senate race in Goiás with 27% of voting intentions, according to a Gerp poll released on April 14, 2026. Deputy Gustavo Gayer (PL) ranks second with 20%, followed by Senator Vanderlan Cardoso (PSD) with 15%. The survey, conducted from April 6 to 10 with 1,206 respondents, has a margin of error of 2.88 percentage points and a 95% confidence level.

item.title: Prêmio de Jornalismo do Poder360 vai para reportagem sobre Lulinha
item.description: The report on the testimony suggesting a link between Fábio Luís Lula da Silva (Lulinha) and the Careca do INSS won the 2nd Poder360 Janio de Freitas Journalism Award. Produced by Mariana Haubert, the story alleged the businessman paid Lulinha a monthly stipend of around R$300 thousand, prompting a public statement from President Lula and later being dismissed by the INSS Parliamentary Inquiry Commission in March 2025.

item.title: Relator ironiza PT sobre PL de apps: “É nocivo garantir Previdência?”
item.description: The rapporteur of the bill regulating app-based work in the Chamber, Augusto Coutinho (Republicanos-PE), mocked the Lula government’s position, asking if 'is it harmful to guarantee Social Security?', after the PT criticized the text as harmful to workers. After pressure from the Planalto, which hardened its stance against the report, Coutinho canceled the vote in the special committee, citing lack of consensus and saying the deadlock is a pity for workers. The government had proposed adjustments, such as a minimum fee of R$ 10, but ultimately opposed the text for flexibilizing rights like night shift pay, holiday payments, and access to algorithms.

item.title: Sem aula, sem salário: professoras temporárias grávidas enfrentam limbo na rede estadual paulista
item.description: Pregnant temporary teachers in São Paulo's public school system, classified under category O, are facing salary suspension and removal from classrooms after changes to assignment and performance evaluation rules by Governor Tarcísio de Freitas. Despite legal provisions for provisional stability, women like Roberta Rieger, with high-risk pregnancies, have been left unpaid even with formal contracts intact, due to new requirements to reapply via the Simplified Selection Process (PSS) after contract terminations. Dieese data shows over 35,000 temporary teachers had contracts terminated, with more than 14,000 affected between December 2025 and February 2026.

item.title: Indicados de Bolsonaro assumem comando do TSE com desafio da IA na eleição
item.description: Kássio Nunes Marques and André Mendonça have taken office as president and vice-president of the TSE, with the use of artificial intelligence during the electoral period identified as the main challenge by electoral law experts consulted by UOL.

item.title: Nexus: Eleitorado 60+ avança e se torna estratégico para eleições no Brasil
item.description: Voters over 60 are growing in number and becoming a strategic segment in Brazil's 2026 elections, driven by rising life expectancy and increased political engagement. Their influence could be decisive in a highly contested race, particularly on issues like pensions, healthcare, and security.

item.title: A personagem de IA que viraliza com críticas ao governo Lula e ao STF
item.description: Dona Maria is an AI-generated avatar that went viral on social media for her sharp criticisms of the Lula government and the STF, portraying an angry elderly Black woman. Her July 2025 video, posted during the U.S. tariff dispute with Brazil, reached 8.8 million views and sparked thousands of comments, highlighting electoral polarization between Lula supporters and Bolsonarists. The case illustrates how AI tools are being deployed to amplify political narratives ahead of the 2026 elections.

item.title: Eleitor de direita vai escolher qualquer um que possa vencer Lula
item.description: Lula appears to have hit his electoral ceiling at 45%, technically tying with right-wing candidates like Flávio Bolsonaro, Caiado, and Zema in recent Datafolha polls. Right-wing voters are willing to support any anti-Lula candidate who can defeat him, signaling significant wear and tear and a lack of a strong alternative in the government camp. In a potential runoff, the right gains an advantage as voters prioritize the ability to beat Lula over party affiliation.

item.title: Oposição busca unidade no dia da votação que pode consolidar vitória do governo no TCU
item.description: The opposition in the Chamber of Deputies is seeking to unite behind a single candidate to challenge Deputy Odair Cunha (PT), the government-backed nominee, in the TCU election. Despite behind-the-scenes talks, opposition candidates remain reluctant to withdraw, fearing it would strengthen a direct rival within their own bloc. The election, held today in a single round with secret ballot, may favor Cunha due to the risk of opposition vote fragmentation.

item.title: Terceirizados têm reembolso-creche e garantia de 40h semanais
item.description: President Lula signed a measure expanding labor rights for federal outsourced workers, including a childcare reimbursement of up to R$ 526,64 per child and a reduction in the workweek from 44 to 40 hours without salary reduction. The policy covers around 40,000 workers and could benefit up to 14,000 children under six, with an estimated monthly cost of R$ 7.5 million, absorbed within existing budgets.

item.title: Avisado pelo STF de que deve ficar no cargo, governador interino do Rio troca postos-chave
item.description: Rio de Janeiro's interim governor, Judge Ricardo Couto, is making key personnel changes after being informed by the STF that he will likely remain in office for several more months, possibly until year-end, as the state’s gubernatorial succession will not be resolved in time for direct elections. His allies say he was warned by STF ministers that he will not be removed soon, underscoring the ongoing uncertainty over the state’s leadership transition.

item.title: Aposta de Boulos, PL dos apps vira impasse para Lula antes da eleição
item.description: The government's effort to regulate app-based work, a key Lula strategy to win over voters ahead of the 2026 election, has stalled in the Chamber of Deputies after rapporteur Augusto Coutinho released a final report that cuts night and Sunday bonuses and removes platform obligations to provide support points. Guilherme Boulos, Minister of the Presidency's General Secretariat, criticized the report as a setback that ignores worker consultations and said the government will not support it. He also urged platforms like Uber and iFood to balance power with workers enduring long hours without basic guarantees.

item.title: Simões aposta que Cleitinho desistirá de eleição em MG: "Vamos ser aliados"
item.description: Minas Gerais Governor Mateus Simões (PSD) stated he believes Senator Cleitinho Azevedo (Republicanos-MG), currently leading in polls, will be his ally rather than opponent in the 2026 election, noting they have never run separately. Simões also mentioned talks with federal deputy Nikolas Ferreira (PL-MG) and openness to a potential alliance between Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) and former governor Romeu Zema (Novo), which could ease his re-election bid.

item.title: TSE troca comando e terá Nunes Marques na presidência nas eleições
item.description: The Superior Electoral Court (TSE) will elect a new presidency in an administrative session scheduled for Tuesday, April 14, confirming Ministers Nunes Marques as president and André Mendonça as vice-president, following the court's tradition. The change follows the early departure of Minister Cármen Lúcia, who chose to leave office before the end of her term to ensure a smooth transition and give the new president more time to prepare for the October elections. With Cármen Lúcia's departure, Minister Dias Toffoli assumes her seat as a titular member of the TSE.

item.title: Mateus Simões torce por Zema vice de Flávio: "Facilitaria minha vida"
item.description: Minas Gerais Governor Mateus Simões (PSD) said an alliance between Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) and Romeu Zema (Novo) as vice president would ease his re-election bid in Minas by resolving uncertainty over PL’s support for his candidacy. He praised Zema’s fiscal management and national leadership potential but stressed he would never ask Zema to join the ticket. Flávio’s campaign is also considering alliances with Cleitinho (Republicanos-MG) or fielding Flávio Roscoe as a standalone candidate in Minas.

item.title: Patrimônio de bilionários na América Latina sobe 500% em 26 anos, diz estudo
item.description: The total wealth of billionaires in Latin America rose 498% from 2000 to 2026, according to the ITO, but after adjusting for U.S. inflation, the real increase was 206%. The study, commissioned by the Brazilian government and coordinated by the Regional Tax Cooperation Platform, advocates for a minimum wealth tax (Imer) to combat tax avoidance by the ultra-rich. A 1% levy on fortunes over US$100 million could yield US$2.8 billion annually for Brazil.

item.title: PSB faz aceno a Haddad em inserção partidária
item.description: The PSB will air a partisan insertion next Wednesday (May 15) supporting Fernando Haddad’s (PT) gubernatorial campaign in São Paulo, featuring Márcio França, the PSB’s Senate pre-candidate, in a simulated phone call highlighting positive economic indicators from the Lula government, such as falling unemployment and controlled inflation. The piece will also revisit França’s personal background, recalling his past work as a fabric store clerk on Rua 25 de Março.

item.title: TSE retoma julgamento que pode cassar chapa de Denarium e Damião
item.description: The TSE resumed the trial that could annul the ticket of Antonio Denarium and Edilson Damião, convicted by the TRE-RR for political and economic abuse in the 2022 elections, including the use of social programs like Cesta da Família and Renda Cidadã to buy votes and distribute R$70 million to allied municipalities. The vote was 2-0 in favor of annulment before Nunes Marques requested a vista; now Ministers Ferreira, Peixoto, Aranha, and Cármen Lúcia will vote. Denarium resigned and is a pre-candidate for Senate, while Damião remains acting governor.

item.title: Para 75% dos brasileiros, STF tem poder demais, diz Datafolha
item.description: According to a Datafolha poll, 75% of Brazilians believe the Supreme Federal Court (STF) has too much power, although 71% consider the Court essential for maintaining democracy. The perception of excessive power is higher among Jair Bolsonaro voters (88%) and lower among Lula supporters (64%). The survey also found that 70% of respondents were aware of suspicions linking STF ministers to the Master Case, of whom 55% believe the ministers are involved.

item.title: Na Presidência do TSE, Nunes Marques vai defender higidez e credibilidade das urnas
item.description: Minister Nunes Marques is set to be elected president of the TSE on Tuesday (14), succeeding Cármen Lúcia and beginning preparations for the 2026 elections. He pledges to personally defend the integrity of electronic voting machines, combat voter abstention, accelerate the removal of harmful AI-generated content, and increase Indigenous participation in the electoral process. André Mendonça will be elected vice-president, and both were nominated to the STF by Jair Bolsonaro, despite his history of unfounded attacks on the electoral system.

item.title: Nunes Marques chega ao comando do TSE prometendo perfil discreto e discurso de pacificação em ano eleitoral
item.description: Minister Nunes Marques of the Supreme Federal Court (STF) is set to be elected president of the Superior Electoral Court (TSE) this Tuesday, promising a discreet, impartial management aimed at reducing political tension in the election year. His appointment follows the early departure of Carmen Lucía, based on seniority, and he will oversee the full organization of the 2026 elections. Known for a low-friction profile and conservative rulings on moral and criminal guarantees, Nunes Marques avoids public confrontations, with André Mendonça as vice-president reinforcing the commitment to discretion and stability.

item.title: TSE retoma julgamento que pode cassar governador de Roraima e levar a novas eleições no estado
item.description: The TSE resumes the trial that could lead to the removal of Roraima's governor, Edilson Damião (Republicans), and trigger new elections in the state, in a case also involving former governor Antonio Denarium (PP). Both are accused of using social programs for electoral gain, transferring funds during prohibited periods, and misusing institutional advertising for personal promotion. Court ministers view the outcome as likely unfavorable, with risks of mandate removal and ineligibility.

item.title: Lula aconselhou Moraes sobre caso Master por respeitá-lo, diz PT
item.description: PT national president Edinho Silva stated that Lula advised Alexandre de Moraes to recuse himself in the Banco Master case out of respect for the minister, aiming to safeguard his legacy and ensure full investigation of allegations. Edinho praised Moraes for having 'fulfilled a magnificent role in defense of democracy' and denied any TCU-related deal or Paraíba candidacy agreement, confirming Lula's support for João Azevêdo and Veneziano Vital do Rêgo.

item.title: Eduardo Bolsonaro lança programa em canal conservador no YouTube
item.description: Eduardo Bolsonaro announced a new weekly program on the Rede Comunica Brasil YouTube channel, set to premiere on April 14, 2026, at 7 a.m. Brasília time. The channel, based in Salvador and focused on Christian and family-oriented content, has 55,000 YouTube subscribers and 91,600 Instagram followers. The program will feature Bahia state deputy Leandro de Jesus (PL) and reflects Eduardo Bolsonaro’s continued reliance on video messaging following his self-exile in the United States since February 2025.

item.title: Deputados se juntam a Seif e pedem asilo político a Ramagem
item.description: Opposition lawmakers, led by Cabo Gilberto (PL), requested political asylum in the U.S. for Alexandre Ramagem, former Abin director and ex-deputy detained by ICE after his visa expired. They claim Ramagem is a political persecutee due to his STF conviction for involvement in the 2023 coup plot. Senator Jorge Seif had previously made the same request.

item.title: Pimenta protocola 3 projetos na estreia como líder de Lula na Câmara
item.description: The new government leader in the Chamber of Deputies, Paulo Pimenta (PT-RS), filed three bills on his first day in office, including regulations for electronic toll-free flow systems, the National Program for Autonomy and Protection of Women in Domestic Violence Situations ('Recomeçar Mulher'), and the 'Single Water Meter Law' to prevent commercial fees on mixed-use residential properties. He replaced José Guimarães as government leader after Guimarães was appointed to the Institutional Relations Secretariat.

item.title: Defesa de Bolsonaro afirma que irmão de Michelle presta apoio doméstico
item.description: Bolsonaro's defense told the STF that Carlos Eduardo Antunes Torres, Michelle Bolsonaro's stepbrother, provides domestic support during the former president's house arrest, not as a professional caregiver but as a trusted family member. The request followed Justice Alexandre de Moraes' demand for professional qualifications, which the defense rejects, citing Torres' long-standing family support since 2018 and familial bond.

item.title: Padilha associa Flávio Bolsonaro a ‘apagão’ em hospitais do RJ e diz que saúde será tema eleitoral
item.description: Health Minister Alexandre Padilha linked Flávio Bolsonaro to the mismanagement of federal hospitals in Rio de Janeiro, claiming the senator was responsible for a true 'blackout' in the state's health system and should not govern the country or the Ministry of Health. He stated that health will be a central theme in the 2026 elections, contrasting the current government's proposals with Bolsonaro's history of negationist stances on vaccination and international health cooperation. Padilha also reinforced Lula's support for Fernando Haddad as the winning candidate in São Paulo, emphasizing the state's decisive role in the 2022 presidential election.

item.title: Oposição no Brasil diz que vai pressionar por asilo a Ramagem nos EUA
item.description: The leader of the opposition in the Brazilian Chamber of Deputies, Cabo Gilberto (PL-PB), announced that the group will pressure the United States to grant political asylum to Alexandre Ramagem, a former deputy and Bolsonaro ally detained by immigration authorities in Orlando after losing his mandate and diplomatic passport. Ramagem has been a fugitive in the U.S. since September 2025, sentenced to 16 years by the STF for his role in the January 8 attacks, and already has an asylum request filed in the U.S., which the opposition seeks to prioritize.

item.title: Comissão da Câmara aprova 7 candidatos ao TCU; plenário vota nesta terça
item.description: The Chamber of Deputies' Finance and Taxation Committee unanimously approved seven candidates for the vacant TCU minister position left by Aroldo Cedraz's retirement. The final decision will be made in a secret ballot in the plenary on Tuesday, with the top vote-getter proceeding to a Senate hearing and vote. Odair Cunha (PT-MG) has the backing of Chamber President Hugo Motta and a coalition of parties including MDB, PT, PDT, PCdoB, PSB, and Republicanos.

item.title: União Brasil em São Paulo ameaça implodir federação com o PP
item.description: The São Paulo branch of União Brasil threatens to dissolve its federation with the PP if Senator Ciro Nogueira (PP-PI) is appointed as the alliance's leader, insisting that São Paulo politics demands local leadership and rejecting rule by proxy. The statement from party president Alexandre Leite warns that if reason does not prevail, the party will escalate the issue to the National Executive and work to permanently dismantle the alliance, causing instability in the electoral process.

item.title: Ramagem foi detido por infração de trânsito, diz Eduardo
item.description: Eduardo Bolsonaro stated that Alexandre Ramagem was detained in the U.S. for a traffic violation, not due to Brazil's extradition request. Ramagem, who has been a fugitive since his conviction for involvement in the coup attempt, is awaiting an asylum hearing in the U.S., with strong expectations of release. Paulo Figueiredo, an ally and partner at Immigrex, confirmed he is providing legal assistance to prevent deportation.

item.title: “Isso vai acabar”, diz Flávio ao comentar prisão de Ramagem
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) commented on the arrest of Alexandre Ramagem by ICE in Orlando, Florida, stating that the former deputy has an ongoing asylum request and is legally well-protected. Flávio said 'this will end', expressing confidence in the reversal of the measure. The statement was posted on X (formerly Twitter).

item.title: Cláudio Castro falta à CPI do Crime Organizado e alega ‘dores na lombar’
item.description: Former Rio de Janeiro governor Cláudio Castro (PL) did not attend the Senate’s Organized Crime CPI hearing on Tuesday, May 14, citing severe lower back pain diagnosed as acute lumbargia. His summons followed his resignation in March, one day before being declared ineligible until 2030 by the TSE. CPI rapporteur Senator Alessandro Vieira (MDB-SE) emphasized Castro’s testimony would be vital to uncovering how state institutions were used to create thousands of irregular public positions to benefit political allies and fund his 2022 re-election campaign.

item.title: Votação de regras para trabalho por aplicativos é adiada e relator cobra governo: 'Quero que o Boulos mande um projeto'
item.description: The vote on the bill regulating app-based work in the Chamber was postponed due to a disagreement between the rapporteur, Deputy Augusto Coutinho, and the federal government, which has shifted to opposing the text. Coutinho accused the government of blocking progress by rejecting the proposed minimum wage of R$ 8.50 for delivery workers, which he supports, while the government advocates for R$ 10. He demanded that Minister of the Presidency's Secretariat, Guilherme Boulos, submit a government proposal so he could vote in favor.

item.title: Após pressão do governo, projeto que regulamenta atividade de entregadores e motoristas sai de pauta na Câmara
item.description: The bill regulating app-based delivery and ride-hailing workers was removed from the Chamber of Deputies' agenda following government pressure, with rapporteur Augusto Coutinho declaring the project 'dead'. The proposal set a minimum of R$8.50 per delivery or R$14.74 per hour, but faced opposition from Minister Guilherme Boulos (PSOL), who advocated for R$10 per trip, and resistance from platforms and workers, resulting in its withdrawal.

item.title: Oposição minimiza caso de Ramagem, contesta PF e diz que ex-deputado passa por “procedimento padrão” após ser detido pelo ICE
item.description: Opposition lawmakers in Congress downplayed the detention of former deputy Alexandre Ramagem in Florida, claiming he was only detained for a traffic violation with an expired driver’s license, not arrested under a STF or PF order. Bolsonarist allies, including Sóstenes Cavalcante and Bia Kicis, denied any international cooperation between the PF and U.S. authorities, calling it a routine immigration procedure and challenging the PF’s credibility. The narrative seeks to detach the case from judicial rulings by Minister Alexandre de Moraes and frame it as standard bureaucratic processing in the U.S.

item.title: Amigo de Lula, Emílio Odebrecht é apontado como fornecedor de carne de paca servida por Janja na Páscoa
item.description: A longtime friend of President Lula, Emilio Odebrecht, was identified as the supplier of paca meat served by Janja at Easter, according to an O Globo report. Odebrecht claims to be Brazil’s largest paca breeder and allegedly gifted the meat to the presidential couple. While no illegality is suggested, the connection raises concerns about potential conflicts of interest given Odebrecht’s historical ties to the Lula administration.

item.title: Lula vê evaporar vantagem sobre concorrentes em pesquisa Datafolha
item.description: A Datafolha poll shows President Lula has lost his lead over rivals in the 2026 elections, entering a technical tie in various second-round scenarios. For the first time, he is numerically surpassed by Flávio Bolsonaro, with 46% voting intention versus 45% for the petista. Against Ronaldo Caiado and Romeu Zema, Lula also scores 45%, while opponents maintain similar percentages.

item.title: Cláudio Castro diz que não irá depor à CPI do Crime Organizado por ‘lombalgia aguda’
item.description: Former Rio de Janeiro governor Cláudio Castro (PL) announced he will not appear before the Senate's Organized Crime CPI due to a diagnosis of acute lumbar pain, which requires him to avoid travel and in-person activities. The summons was approved after his resignation in March, as the STF had previously ruled that sitting governors cannot be summoned to CPI hearings. Castro was declared ineligible until 2030 by the TSE and is accused of using state agencies to create over 27,000 irregular appointed positions to benefit political allies and support his 2022 re-election bid.

item.title: Cármen Lúcia diz que é aconselhada a deixar o STF por ataques machistas
item.description: Minister Cármen Lúcia of the STF revealed that her family advises her to leave the position due to daily misogynistic and sexist attacks she endures. She noted that the hostile environment against women in the Court is so severe that some judges may refuse to join the Supreme Court out of fear of becoming targets. Despite the pressure, she insists she acts strictly within the law, while her family urges her to step down, saying she has already fulfilled her duty.

item.title: PF investiga governador de Roraima como chefe de esquema de fraudes
item.description: The Federal Police is investigating Roraima's governor, Edilson Damião (União Brasil), as the suspected leader of a fraud scheme in state infrastructure contracts, directing tenders to specific companies like C B Pedra Serviços e Construções and leaking bid results to allies before official publication. The probe also identifies former Civil Affairs chief Disney Barreto Mesquita as the head of the scheme's 'financial arm', allegedly laundering money through fuel stations and hotels. Damião assumed office in March 2026 after Antonio Denarium resigned to run for Senate, and both will face trial at the TSE on April 14 for abuse of power in the 2022 elections.

item.title: União Brasil em SP critica articulação para Ciro Nogueira liderar federação com PP e fala em risco de ruptura
item.description: The São Paulo branch of União Brasil opposed the proposal for Senator Ciro Nogueira (PP-PI) to lead the upcoming União Progressista federation, stating that leadership must reflect local realities. The party criticized negotiations with the PP as potentially covert and warned it would escalate the issue to the National Executive if unresolved, to prevent instability in the 2026 electoral project.
